Arrr, in Ruby ye can upcase a string with `upcase`, matey: `name = "ahoy"; name.upcase` gives `"AHOY"`.  
If ye want to change the original string in place, use `upcase!`: `name.upcase!`.
how to split a string in Ruby

Arrr, use Ruby’s `split` matey: `parts = "a,b,c".split(",")` gives ye `["a", "b", "c"]`.  
If ye don’t pass a separator, it splits on whitespace: `"ahoy matey".split` becomes `["ahoy", "matey"]`.  
Ye can also limit the pieces: `"a,b,c".split(",", 2)` gives `["a", "b,c"]`.
